chapters.title: Boot Camp
chapters.subtitle: Sequencing & Loops
chapters.intro: Your robot does exactly what you say: no more, no less, and never what you meant. Write instructions in order, squash repetition with loops, and keep an eye on the two numbers that will haunt you all semester: HP and stamina.
objectives: Trace a sequence step by step
Reason about turns relative to facing
Predict HP and stamina costs
Use repeat, and see that nested loops multiply
Compare the cost of two plans

chapters.title: Eyes Open
chapters.subtitle: Conditionals & Sensors
chapters.intro: A program that only works on the map you've already seen is just a recording. Sensors, if/else and while let one program handle maps it has never met. Every level now ships several maps, and your program must pass all of them, exactly like a test suite.
objectives: Use indefinite iteration and loop guards
Branch, including nested branches
Cover every case in a decision
Treat map variants as test cases
Read failures as evidence

chapters.title: Name It, Reuse It
chapters.subtitle: Functions & Recursion
chapters.intro: Your programs are getting long and repetitive. Functions let you name an idea once and use it anywhere, facing any direction. Recursion lets a function call itself, and the call stack quietly remembers things you have no variable for.
objectives: Decompose a task into functions
Choose where to draw a function's boundary
Compose functions that call functions
Write recursion with a base case
Use the call stack as memory
Recognize and explain a stack overflow

chapters.title: Lost in the Labyrinth
chapters.subtitle: Maze Algorithms
chapters.intro: Real mazes fight back with loops, dead ends, fog and stingy batteries. Go from a wall-hugging rule of thumb to depth-first search with an explicit stack, then to breadth-first search that floods the maze with distances, and finally (bonus) Dijkstra, for when steps don't all cost the same.
objectives: Tell a heuristic from a correct algorithm
Use a visited set
Compare a stack (LIFO) with a queue (FIFO)
Argue that DFS finds an exit and BFS finds a shortest path
Explore an unknown map vs. plan on a known one
Work with weighted graphs and priority queues
